tagline: The sheltered lagoon of Walvis Bay, the resort coast of Swakopmund and the wildlife waters of Lüderitz.
summary: Namibia's marine-mobility opportunity sits on a cold, dramatic Atlantic coast where the usable water is sheltered. Walvis Bay, the principal port, holds a large protected lagoon famous for flamingos and the Pelican Point seal colony, with the resort town of Swakopmund just north. Far to the south, Lüderitz shelters behind Diaz Point with penguin colonies on Halifax Island. The Benguela current keeps the sea cold and foggy and the open coast carries swell, so operation centres on the Walvis Bay lagoon and the Lüderitz bays. It is a lagoon-and-wildlife starter market anchored on Walvis Bay.
why_marine_mobility: Namibia's protected water is the Walvis Bay lagoon and the Lüderitz bays, where the sea is calm behind the points while the open Atlantic is cold and swell-prone. Navier's Pioneer II flies these sheltered wildlife-and-harbour hops silent and zero-emission — a clear upgrade on the diesel catamarans that run the Pelican Point and Halifax Island wildlife trips — with the cold, foggy open coast keeping the core opportunity inside the bays.

demand_signals.label: Walvis Bay port & lagoon
demand_signals.note: Walvis Bay is Namibia's principal port with a large sheltered lagoon famous for flamingos and the Pelican Point seal colony, drawing a steady wildlife-tourism market.

demand_signals.label: Swakopmund resort coast
demand_signals.note: Swakopmund, just north of Walvis Bay, is Namibia's leading coastal resort town and adventure-tourism hub.

demand_signals.label: Lüderitz & Halifax Island
demand_signals.note: The southern port of Lüderitz shelters behind Diaz Point with penguin colonies on Halifax Island, a remote wildlife-and-heritage draw on protected bays.

use_cases.body: Silent, zero-emission wildlife runs across the Walvis Bay lagoon to Pelican Point and the seal colony, upgrading the diesel catamaran trips.
A clean harbour-and-lagoon tier linking Walvis Bay and Swakopmund on the sheltered near-shore water.
Wildlife-and-heritage runs on the Lüderitz bays to Halifax Island and Diaz Point on protected southern water.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The Walvis Bay lagoon hops — the town waterfront, Pelican Point and the Swakopmund near-shore run (~18 nm) — and the Lüderitz bays sit within the 70 nm all-electric range on sheltered water, needing only a berth pedestal.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: The bays are Pioneer II territory; the long, cold, swell-exposed open coast between Walvis Bay and Lüderitz (~250 nm) is a Quanta-LR hybrid corridor far beyond all-electric range and beyond the near-shore starter scope.

signature_routes.label: Walvis Bay ↔ Pelican Point (lagoon wildlife run)

transit_planning: For Namibia's port authority (Namport) or an Erongo regional authority: a clean, zero-emission water tier on the Walvis Bay lagoon and the Lüderitz bays, additive to road, as a wildlife-and-harbour starter network.
competitive_landscape: The Walvis Bay and Lüderitz wildlife trips run on diesel catamarans, and there is no scheduled fast passenger service on the lagoon or between the coastal towns. There is no foiling or zero-emission tier on the sheltered water, leaving greenfield room on the calm bays behind the points.
regulatory_note: Marine activity falls under Namibia's port authority (Namport) and the maritime administration, with the sheltered Walvis Bay lagoon and Lüderitz bays simplifying near-shore operation while the cold, foggy, swell-prone open Atlantic keeps operation inside the bays. Marine-protected wildlife areas require conservation coordination.
seasonality: The Benguela current keeps the Namibian coast cold and frequently foggy year-round, with the strongest south-westerly winds and swell in the September–December spring; the sheltered Walvis Bay lagoon and Lüderitz bays remain operable through the year, calmest in the autumn (March–May) mornings before the afternoon wind.
